reason: Learned latency predictor is user-space Python and easy to extend with new operators/models, but the headline cross-GPU generalization claim needs GPUs we do not have, so only the single-A5000 slice is verifiable.

Fully reproduced AE with user-space linker/loader work on SQLite/memcached/MariaDB, but the heterogeneous-ISA case study cannot be run here so an improvement must target the instrumentation-isolation use case.
CPU-only memory-footprint work with a linked repo; sits on the memory/compression edge of OS topics and the rule-based compression is a fairly closed algorithmic result.

Intra-process resource partitioning via custom dynamic linking is genuine user-space resource management on exactly this class of node; main risks are a per-user clang/LLVM build and unknown artifact completeness.
KV-cache eviction for decode is core LLM-serving memory management and single-GPU by nature; the cost is GPU-hours of long-context accuracy evaluation to defend any policy swap.
Single-node CPU compression inside a ML runtime with clear perf hypotheses, but the code is buried in the very large Apache SystemDS tree rather than a standalone artifact.
Numerics/quantization-emulation library rather than resource management, and the accelerator half of the evaluation is unreachable; only the software emulation path runs here.
Learned query optimization from Google with a real artifact and Postgres integration, but query-optimizer ML is far from the OS-course core per the anchors.
CPU-only lossless matrix compression with memory/IO reduction, but the artifact is a reproducibility-repo subdirectory over the large SystemDS codebase.
Single-node recommendation inference acceleration with a GitHub plus Zenodo artifact; it is a compiler/data-layout contribution rather than a resource-management one.
Mostly an ML/UDF-synthesis data-management application depending on LLM API access and video datasets; little OS resource-management content.
Single-node log-structured versioned storage engine with a replay harness is squarely a storage-engine project; the linked repo is the evaluation harness so artifact completeness needs checking.
Pure user-space SFI, but building Firefox plus a custom WASM/SFI toolchain in 10 weeks with noisy browser benchmarks on a shared host is a very heavy and risky lift.
GNN partitioning has a genuine single-GPU story, but the largest graphs will not fit 24 GB and the artifact is a research compute framework of unknown completeness.
Tiny CPU-only data-structure library that would run trivially here, but no repo was located, which violates the hard requirement.
QEMU TCG needs no root and the ARM/RISC-V to x86 directions run here, but only half the configuration matrix is reachable and TCG-based PARSEC runs are slow.
No repo located and the contribution is a domain-specific time-series encoder, leaving little OS-systems substance to extend.
SLO-aware cross-job resource allocation is a core scheduling problem with obvious policy swaps, but the Ray-Serve-on-Kubernetes stack must be replaced by a local Ray cluster or the trace simulator.
The Bayesian tuner itself is user-space, but the paper's 45-TaskManager three-machine Flink setup cannot be reproduced on 16 cores, so all results need aggressive scale-down.
GPU-memory management for concurrent models fits one A5000 with an artificially constrained budget; repo is a research prototype and the edge framing needs restating.
Co-running preprocessing with training is real GPU resource sharing and the cost model is per-GPU, but the paper's framing and artifact are multi-GPU DLRM with heavy data dependencies.
Prompt/KV caching plus cache-aware scheduling would be an ideal topic, but no repo was located so the improvement would have to be built from scratch.
CPU-GPU data placement is a decent single-node memory-management angle, but no artifact was found.
Video-analytics front-end and pipeline optimizer runs fine on one GPU, but the contribution is language/API design rather than OS resource management.
Energy-vs-time tradeoff is a real resource-management knob with a maintained repo, but NVML power-limit setting normally needs root so only batch-size and job-level knobs are safely reachable.
Pure user-space Python autotuner with open source and lots of room for acquisition-function or search-space swaps, but autotuning search is systems-adjacent rather than core OS.

Available+Functional+Reproduced artifact whose workloads fit this RAM and disk; the core is an ORAM/index co-design closer to security than to OS resource management, and network results must be emulated in-process.
Elastic GPU-memory ballooning across co-served models is exactly the single-24GB-GPU regime, kvcached is released and maintained, and the ballooning policy is a clean hypothesis surface.
The coding core is a user-space ISA-L library studiable with local microbenchmarks, but the end-to-end HDFS cluster numbers become pseudo-distributed and distort the seek/network balance.
Single-machine user-space KV retrieval with a learned index, but it lives inside the large mpc4j crypto library and the security framing dilutes the systems angle.
Dedicated artifact repo for user-space libpulp patching, but it may still need privileges to attach, and a live-patching measurement study offers a narrow improvement surface.
CPU-only and cheap to run, but no artifact was found and the contribution is a sampling trade-off study rather than a system.

GC/tail-latency in user-space JVMs is a great OS topic and cgroup v2 is delegated, but the artifact demands a dual-socket 32-core-per-socket NUMA machine with hyper-threading disabled, which needs root and hardware we lack.
A Python simulator plus single-host multi-process LogCabin runs would be feasible, but no official repo is confirmed and consensus-protocol correctness is outside the OS-resource-management core.
No PDF, no abstract, and no artifact yet; the evaluation likely targets production distributed services we cannot recreate.
Self-contained user-space C++ library that builds and benchmarks trivially here, but a succinct-data-structure result has little OS resource-management content.
Released figshare traces mean the expensive cross-device profiling is already done and predictor training fits one A5000; it is a learned cost model, so systems-adjacent rather than core.
No official repo and the design is motivated by 10k-node MoE training, so both the artifact and the regime are out of reach.
Co-scheduling foreground reads against compaction is a textbook LSM resource-management problem with obvious policy variants, but a Cassandra ring must be faked as several JVMs on one host.
Memory-efficient multi-model serving on one 24 GB GPU is the perfect regime, but no preprint or artifact exists yet, which is disqualifying under the hard requirement.
Learned cardinality estimation for path queries is the anchor example of a low-os_fit topic, and no repo was located.

Single-GPU attention engine with Ampere support and easy vLLM/SGLang baselines, but it is a large fast-moving upstream CUDA project where a meaningful kernel-level improvement in 10 weeks is hard and some kernels target Hopper.

Hierarchical KV-cache manager that offloads cold pages to host memory is ideal for one 24 GB GPU plus 125 GiB RAM, with a Zenodo artifact and an obvious space of classification/offload-policy variants.
Syscall-usage analysis for OS compatibility layers is genuinely OS-flavored user-space tooling with a public results database; the main cost is porting the Docker harness to conda/bwrap.
Offline trace-volume reduction would run fine on CPU, but no official repo was found and the production traces may not be public.

A parallel discrete-event simulator explicitly targeting single-node multicore scaling matches this Threadripper, with clear thread-management and synchronization hypotheses; deps must be hand-installed from the Docker workspace.
All the scheduling logic lives in a single-GPU serving loop with a draft/target pair that fits 24 GB and no FP8 dependence; artifact completeness of the research repo is the open question.
A genuine cache admission and staleness-bound contribution integrated into pgvector, with obvious predicate and refresh-policy swaps; repo completeness and dataset size are unverified.

Cache and compute servers both run as local processes on this host, the DataFusion/Rust artifact looks real, and the transcoding format plus eviction policy are natural improvement targets (Rust must be installed in user space).
No artifact found, and predictive frame sampling for video views is an application-level ML question rather than systems resource management.
Single-GPU compiler fusion work that would fit the machine, but no official repo was found by search.
Work must stay inside the released trace-driven simulator since PTZ cameras and Mahimahi are unavailable, and the datasets sit on Dropbox; the topic is video-analytics accuracy, not OS resources.
Mature open-source user-space compiler with 80+ CPU kernel benchmarks that run here, but a scheduling-language design paper is far from OS resource management.

Zenodo artifact is a CPU-only simulator plus carbon traces, so policy swaps are cheap and testable; it is a limitations study, so the project must be framed as improving the policy rather than a speedup.
Page-frame allocation is core memory management with a fully reproduced AE and a standalone user-space Rust benchmark, but the strongest claims need the patched kernel we cannot boot.
CPU-only checker with a public corpus and an artifact appendix, but a static type system offers only checking-speed or precision as an 'improvement', which is a weak systems hypothesis.
Ampere tensor cores are supported and it is a clean single-GPU artifact, but sparse-kernel format engineering is a numerical-library contribution rather than an OS one.
Chiplet-aware task placement is real scheduling and this very Threadripper PRO is multi-CCD, but a substantial part of the analysis relies on hardware counters that perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks.
Memory tiering for SSD-KV indices is a good topic done in user space, but no repo was located and the setup emulates a special memory device.

Single-GPU CUDA Datalog engine runs here in principle, but some datasets exceed 24 GB, the exact artifact branch is unclear, and the contribution is a query-engine data structure rather than OS resource management.
Single-node LSM MVCC with data separation and concurrent memtable flushing is a core storage-engine problem with tunable policies; artifact completeness is unverified.

Lossless tensor compression to cut PCIe transfer is exactly the one-GPU-plus-PCIe setting of this machine and the artifact is available; compression-scheme and placement variants are natural hypotheses.
Extremely reproducible CPU/SIMD artifact, but vector quantization with error bounds is an algorithms/ANN contribution with little OS content.
Unified open framework makes reproduction easy, but the billion-scale datasets need scale-down and an evaluation paper leaves mostly 'add another index' as the extension.
A CacheLib flash-cache module for tiny objects runs entirely in user space on the local NVMe, and set-associative admission/write-amplification policies are an obvious, well-defined hypothesis space.
No repo located and a metric-space learned index is a narrow indexing result far from OS resource management.
A learned filter over sliding windows is a plausible data-structure project on CPU, but no artifact was found.
Network-configuration verification is outside the OS-resource-management scope, the industrial case study is unreleasable, and only runtime/memory on public topologies remains.

Preemptive GPU scheduling as a user-space shim over the CUDA driver API with an Available+Functional+Reproduced artifact and Zenodo DOI; only the one Ampere GPU is available and the top hardware-preemption level may be unreachable on driver 535.

The bandwidth-versus-load heuristic can be studied purely by simulation here, but the released prototype is a ~10-node distributed repair system whose end-to-end timings will be distorted on one host.
Pure in-memory CPU index that runs effortlessly on this machine, but the note is thin about artifact completeness and a temporal index is a fairly self-contained data-structure result.
Prefix KV-cache eviction with both a trace-driven simulator and a vLLM implementation on one 24 GB GPU is the ideal shape: swap the eviction policy, re-run the simulator, validate end to end.

The A5000 does have RT cores and OptiX so the mechanism reproduces, but it is a largely negative GPU-microarchitecture case study that suits only the reproduction fallback, with driver-version and 24 GB graph-size risks.
Open-source single-GPU compiler from Alibaba, but it is tied to an aging TensorFlow/XLA stack that may be painful to build against CUDA 11.8 and driver 535.

Production-quality Rust KV engine using the WAL as permanent storage on NVMe is core storage-systems work with clear relocation/compaction hypotheses; the 1 TB experiment must shrink to 257 GB of free space.
Single-GPU Ampere-supported artifact with a Zenodo benchmark archive and a clean gsplat baseline, but 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering is a graphics application, not OS resource management.
A pure-Python white-box discrete-event simulator for provisioning, caching and scheduling policies is exactly the trace-driven policy study this machine supports, with cheap policy-swap hypotheses.

Serverless GPU elasticity and co-scaling is core resource management and the mechanism is per-GPU, but the paper's cluster framing and likely container/serverless plumbing must be rebuilt without Docker or root.

A llama.cpp-derived engine that rebalances hot/cold FFN neuron groups between one GPU and host CPU targets exactly 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM + 16 cores, and the balancing policy is a clean hypothesis surface.
A modular scheduler simulator validated by reproducing prior policies from traces needs no cluster hardware and makes new-policy prototyping cheap - close to an ideal 10-week improvement target.
